youtube.title: Big Walk Used AI for 10 Lines of Code and Judges Noticed
youtube.description: Big Walk's studio House House says generative AI touched well under 0.1 percent of the game's code, and 19 Independent Games Festival jurors now refuse to vote for any game that used it at all. The studio posted the disclosure on its own FAQ, said it is not an endorsement and called its missing AI policy a failure. Here is what the row means for one of the year's best-liked indies. Sources: PC Gamer, GameSpot, VGC, Eurogamer, Rock Paper Shotgun, GamesIndustry.biz, Nintendo Life.
title_variants: Big Walk Studio Admits AI Helped Fix One Bug
19 IGF Jurors Won't Vote for AI Games, and Big Walk Used Some

claims.claim: House House estimates well under 0.1% of Big Walk's code had anything to do with LLM usage.
The example given was about 10 lines of code used to fix a problem House House could not fix manually or with a Unity engineer.
19 IGF jurors said they are declining to vote for any game that uses generative AI in any capacity.
House House made no disclosure on Steam because the platform does not request disclosure of code or chatbot usage.
House House posted the disclosure on the Big Walk website FAQ.
House House said the lack of an internal AI usage policy was a failure.
House House said the statement is not an endorsement of AI tools.
LLMs were used in the final stretch of development to work through difficult technical challenges and bugs.

issues.quote: Big Walk Used AI for 10 Lines of Code and Judges Noticed
issues.problem: The title compresses the story into 'used AI for 10 lines of code', but the sources describe the ~10 lines as one example (PC Gamer: 'about 10 lines of code' to fix one problem) within a broader 'well under 0.1%' estimate across 'some cases'; the title risks implying 10 lines was the total. The script itself correctly says '10 lines for one bug', so this is a headline simplification rather than a factual error.

issues.quote: the studio outed itself. That's disclosure, not a scandal.
issues.problem: Framed as opinion and the studio did post the disclosure itself, but Eurogamer characterises it as done 'under pressure' after social media claims; 'outed itself' slightly flatters the voluntariness. Opinion, not a blocker.

check.summary: All core claims (AI used sparingly, under 0.1% of code, ~10-line bug-fix example, 19 IGF jurors declining to vote for gen-AI games, Steam not requesting code/chatbot disclosure, 'failure' quote about the missing policy, FAQ posting) are supported by the sources. On-screen text and description check out. Only minor issues: the YouTube title's '10 Lines of Code' compression and the opinion framing of the studio 'outing itself'. Correctly not labelled as rumour since the disclosure is confirmed.
